item.description:

item.title: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years as anger over housing leads to clashes
item.description:
A protester holds a "housing is a right, not a business" sign during a demonstration in Barcelona on Nov. 11, 2026. —Davide Bonaldo—SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty Images Millions of workers on Wednesday staged Spain’s first general strike in 14 years in protest of the country’s housing crisis . Around 4 million workers—around 17% of the country’s 23 million-strong workforce—participated in the Nov. 11 walkout, unions said. The strike was organized by Spain’s two largest unions, the General Union of Workers (UGT) and the Workers’ Commissions (CCOO), tenants’ associations, and other unions. In cities across Spain, including Barcelona, Madrid, and Valencia, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets on Wednesday to demand measures to bring down rental prices. The last nationwide general strike was in 2012, when workers staged nationwide walkouts and downed tools to protest…

item.title: Famed ship SS United States deliberately sunk off Florida coast to become a reef
item.description:
SS United States, which set transatlantic speed record during maiden voyage in 1952, is sunk off coast of Destin The historic SS United States has reached the end of its journey at sea, sinking Wednesday off the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will begin a new life underwater as an artificial reef. The nearly 1,000ft American-made vessel, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, was launched in 1952 and made history by setting a transatlantic speed record during its maiden voyage. The ship carried thousands of passengers across the Atlantic over 17 years of operation before being retired in 1969. Continue reading...

item.title: Australian teen found alive after six days in the bush
item.description:
An 11-month-old South Carolina baby who was buried alive for roughly 24 hours in a dog crate was found “clinging to life” Tuesday following an extensive search and rescue effort. Koah Sharpe was reported missing on Monday after his father, Michael Comer, allegedly took him from his grandmother’s care. Comer was later arrested on a burglary charge, but the infant remained missing. “We found some video early this morning of Michael around in and around Batesburg-Leesville, with no baby,” Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon told reporters. “So certainly we got worried, hoping and praying that he dropped a baby with another person.” Comer had no vehicle and no Amber Alert was issued. Nearly 100 first responders joined the frantic search to locate Koah, according to Koon. item.title: The Hegseth Impeachment is Far From Over
item.description:
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. (Daniel Torok / B66 / Avalon/Newscom) Today, House Republicans managed to block the impeachment of Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, by voting 211-204 to send it to a committee for further "study." But this fight is likely to be far from over. The Republicans may be able to effectively bottle up the impeachment in committee for the rest of the current Congress (which ends on January 3, 2027). But it will almost certainly come back in the new Democratic-controlled Congress. With approximately 260 seats in the new House, the Democrats (virtually all of whom support impeachment) should easily be able to vote to impeach. item.title: Thousands of schools evacuated in Italy as bomb threats spread across Europe
item.description:
Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts across Europe in recent weeks, which have prompted growing concern about the possibility of an escalation in hybrid warfare.

item.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, 42-day countdown to 'Ebola-free' begins
item.description:
Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, who has now officially recovered. The 11 other people who had been in quarantine were also released from hospital on Wednesday, November 11, as the country began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free. FRANCE 24's Nairobi correspondent Bastien Renouil reports.

item.title: Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia reacts to White House warning
item.description:
CNN, Reuters CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins has sounded the alarm on a new post-midterms threat from the White House. On Wednesday, White House counsel Will Scharf sent a letter to incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia to warn about potential Democratic investigations, saying they may amount to “blatant criminality.” The investigations flagged in the letter, obtained by Punchbowl News , involve congressional Democrats who the White House claims will issue subpoenas to “harass, threaten and deter” Trump administration officials from carrying out their duties, as well as potentially targeting the president’s family. Read more at The Daily Beast.

item.title: Climate progressives won the midterms without saying ‘climate’
item.description:
On October 20, the two candidates running to represent Michigan in the U.S. Senate, Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers, took questions for an hour at the Detroit Economic Club. El-Sayed, the Democrat who had previously run for governor, made a name for himself years ago by connecting public health to the climate crisis. He published a fierce defense of the Green New Deal at the time, touting its economic, health, and planetary benefits . But last month at the Detroit Economic Club, El-Sayed didn’t mention the Green New Deal at all.
